$comment: Platform budget: the shell is what an adopter ships on day one, so its budget must survive the reference strip. Resource budgets are hard failures; lab timing metrics are warnings. See ADR 0009 (not yet authored -- flagged as a Task 8 follow-up, out of this task's file scope) for the full baseline table and the principle below. LIMITATION: every resource-summary assertion below is maxNumericValue -- an upper bound only. @lhci/cli 0.15.1's assertion vocabulary is exactly {minScore, maxLength, maxNumericValue} (verified against node_modules/@lhci/utils/src/assertions.js; minNumericValue is never destructured there, confirmed again by `grep -rl minNumericValue node_modules/.pnpm/` returning nothing while the same grep for maxNumericValue returns two files, proving the search itself works). A build that emits nothing therefore passes every maxNumericValue line here (0 <= any budget), and categories:accessibility at minScore 1 is not a substitute floor either: a syntactically valid, fully empty page (lang, viewport, title, one text node, zero scripts) scores a perfect 1.0. That floor is enforced by composition instead, but the composition must run in the same CI job against the same artifact to mean anything: the `lighthouse` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml builds with VITE_SENTRA_MOCKS=true, which is a different turbo cache key and therefore a different apps/shell/dist tree than the plain `pnpm build` the separate `verify` job's own `Check bundle sizes` step protects (see task-8-report.md's Step 1b for the two build hashes). An earlier version of this task treated `verify`'s bundle-size gate as covering this file's build; it does not, because the two jobs never share a dist. The fix is a `Check bundle sizes` step inside this same `lighthouse` job, immediately after its own Build step and before either Lighthouse invocation, so scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs's classify()/evaluate() run against the exact tree Lighthouse is about to measure -- verified by emptying apps/shell/dist and re-running it: classify()/evaluate() fail loudly ('dist does not exist' / 'budget matched no file'). BASELINE (measured 2026-08-30 from a forced, mocked build, numberOfRuns=1, http://127.0.0.1:4175/): total 293881B/25 requests, script 287967B/20, stylesheet 4809B/1, document 1105B/1, image 0B/0, third-party 0B/0, LCP 674.5ms, TBT 0ms, CLS 0, accessibility 1.0, best-practices 0.96. A budget's value is its distance from this baseline, not its raw size, so each line below is justified on its own terms rather than copied from a formula: script:size (400000, ~1.4x headroom) is left loose deliberately -- tight enough to catch a bad dependency landing, loose enough for normal growth; tightening it to a literal measured+15% (~340000) would make it fire on ordinary feature growth instead. stylesheet:size (5632) uses bundle-budgets.json's own convention (round the measured byte count up to the next whole KB, then +10%) since the placeholder 80000 was 16x the real 4809B and would not fire until something had already gone badly wrong. image:size (0) and third-party:count (0) are pinned to the exact measured value, not padded -- the shell ships zero images and zero third-party requests today, so either one appearing is a deliberate decision that must consciously raise this number rather than slide in under a stale ceiling; third-party:count was already built this way, image:size is now made consistent with it instead of hiding a real property (no images) behind a 500000-byte ceiling that could never fire. total:size (410000) is derived as the sum of the per-type ceilings above plus a small allowance for the unbudgeted document/other categories -- not measured-total+15% (~338000) -- so it can never become the binding constraint ahead of a dedicated per-type budget (a page that legitimately used its full 400000 script:size budget would already exceed a 338000 total ceiling with zero stylesheet or document bytes at all). largest-contentful-paint (800ms) is measured+15%, rounded up to the nearest 50ms. total-blocking-time (50ms) and cumulative-layout-shift (0.02) deliberately exceed a literal measured-zero-plus-15%-equals-zero: both are warn-only lab metrics, and a hard zero would warn on a single millisecond of scheduler jitter or a fraction of a pixel of shift on a shared CI runner, which signals runner noise rather than a regression -- a small explicit tolerance is recorded here rather than silently defaulting to zero and generating noise every run. categories:accessibility (minScore 1) and third-party:count (0) have zero headroom by construction and are the tightest gates in this file; they are passing on merit against the baseline above, not because nothing was measured. A related gap -- index.html referencing a renamed or missing entry script -- is closed by a different composition, not by this file: `apps/shell/e2e-platform-only/platform-only.smoke.spec.ts`, run by the `platform-only` CI job's 'Smoke-check the stripped shell boots in a browser' step (pnpm --filter @sentra/shell e2e:platform-only). Verified, not assumed: renaming the built entry script referenced by dist/index.html and re-running that spec against the broken dist (server started manually so Playwright's reuseExistingServer would not silently rebuild over the injected defect) produced 'platform chrome did not render; captured console/page errors: [...404 (Not Found)...]' -- a distinct, diagnostic failure, not a false pass. See task-8-report.md's Fix round 1 for the full transcript.
